criteria.text: Patient enrollment is by referral only.
All patients must have a pre-operative imaging (CT, MR, or PET scan) available in digital format.
Age is greater than or equal to 18 years.
The patient does not have a serious concurrent medical illness that would preclude making a rational informed decision on participation.
The patient has the ability to understand and willingness to sign a written informed consent form, and to comply with the protocol.

All patients in non-prostate biopsy cohorts must be undergoing an image-guided surgical or interventional radiology procedure such as an angiography or a CT/ US-guided biopsy as clinically indicated or IRB-approved under a separate research protocol.
Patients have undergone a prostate MRI and have had abnormalities identified.
PSA is >2.5 OR digital rectal exam is abnormal OR an abnormality is identified on prostate MRI with a clinical indication for fusion biopsy.
Pre-biopsy prostate MRI shows targetable lesions.
The patient has an altered mental status that precludes understanding or consenting for the biopsy procedure.
The patient is unlikely able to hold reasonably still on a procedure table for the length of the procedure.
The patient has an inability to hold breath, if the procedure will be performed with conscious sedation, and without general anesthesia.
The patient has pacemakers and other potentially electrically conductive implants.
Gross body weight is above the CT table limit (606 pounds), if CT table used.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Use of Tracking Devices to Locate Abnormalities During Invasive Procedures". I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 38 years old, so I am definitely 18 or older.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have any serious ongoing medical conditions that might make it hard for you to understand the study details or make a decision about joining?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have any conditions that would affect my understanding or decision-making. I just know I have cancer and I'm working full-time.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us clarify, do you have any serious ongoing health issues (like heart, lung, or kidney disease) that you know of? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have heart, lung, or kidney disease. I know the cancer spread to my lungs and liver, but I don't have info on other organ issues.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you comfortable reading and signing a written consent form, and do you feel able to follow the study instructions?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I can read and sign forms, and I feel able to follow instructions. I'm working full-time, so I need to make sure I can manage the schedule.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently scheduled for an image-guided procedure, such as a biopsy or angiography, to help locate abnormalities?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I'm scheduled for an image-guided procedure right now. My oncologist is starting topotecan while I look for a clinical trial, but I don't have details on specific upcoming procedures.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a prostate MRI recently, and if so, did the results show any abnormalities?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know, as I am a woman with cervical cancer, so I don't have a prostate.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To make sure you can fully understand and consent to the procedure, do you currently have any confusion, memory issues, or other changes in your mental status that might affect your ability to participate?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have any confusion or memory issues. I just know I have cancer and I'm working full-time.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. During medical procedures, are you able to hold reasonably still on the procedure table for the entire length of the procedure?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I can do light work, but heavy things tire me, so I'm not sure if I can hold still for the entire length of a procedure.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, do you think you would be able to stay completely still on the table for the entire procedure, or do you expect to need to move or shift positions?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I can stay completely still for the entire procedure. I can do light work, but heavy things tire me, so I might need to shift positions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. If the procedure uses conscious sedation (you stay awake but relaxed) without general anesthesia, are you able to hold your breath when asked?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I can hold my breath when asked. I know I get tired from heavy things, but I don't have specific information about my ability to hold my breath during a procedure.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have a pacemaker or any other implants that might conduct electricity, such as a neurostimulator or cochlear implant?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have a pacemaker or any other implants. I haven't mentioned having any devices like that in my history.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your weight is over 606 pounds? This is the limit for the CT table if it is used for the procedure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my weight is over 606 pounds. I haven't mentioned my specific weight in my history.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
